prompt: Create ONE horizontal illustrated strip asset for The Vegetable Guru front cover. Images 1 and 2 are authoritative APPROVED HOUSE STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: bold simplified dimensional botanical drawing, crisp silhouettes, broad discrete overlapping green colour and shadow planes, selective tapered cream graphic highlights, simplified lobed leaves, warm lively natural shapes. Do not copy their background glow, subject arrangement, peppers or large striped marrow. Image 3 is the SELECTED REAL-PHOTO COMPOSITION SOURCE, by Pollinator. Translate the observed arrangement into that exact illustration language. Keep one clearly recognisable long dark-green courgette lying almost horizontally, with its stem attached at left, fruit curving slightly downwards to the rounded right end, like the source. It is the dominant subject. Retain the source's asymmetrical foliage: two or three broad partly overlapping lobed leaves towards the left edge, one much smaller leaf at upper right, just a few naturally angled or curving supporting stalks. A single SMALL, folded golden-yellow flower sits above and left of the fruit, as in the source; make it no more than one quarter of the fruit's length, a secondary accent, not an open starburst. Omit the dirt, leaf damage, dry debris, fine vein networks, crowded foreground crossing stalks, and background. Use the photograph's irregular relationships and perspective, not a decorative symmetrical bouquet or an evenly spaced produce line. Main long fruit should span roughly x650 to x1870 in the 2200px canvas, with leaves at left balancing it. Aim for a SHALLOW WIDE LANDSCAPE composition 2200x680 pixels. Main body occupies the upper 500px, spans almost the full width and may naturally bleed at the top or side edges. Its lower silhouette is organically shaped, NOT a straight rectangular crop. Below y500 keep the central 65 percent completely transparent so the title below has breathing room. Only one modest leaf tip at the far left and a small curved stalk at the far right may trail down to about y610. Do not fill every gap: negative spaces between leaves and stalks must be truly transparent. Transparent background, no paper, no cream or green rectangle, no haze, no ground shadow, no text, labels, border, mockup or book. Avoid photorealism, photographic gloss, soft watercolour, pencil texture, tiny stippling, heavy black outlines, luminous halos, and intricate fine veins. Draw the courgette using a few confident forest/lime green planes and restrained cream highlight slashes, keeping its organic curve and visual volume. One coherent natural growing plant fragment, fruit first, a calm composition suitable above a large book title.
